mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k per month signals strong labor market demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds 200.0 for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to outperform baseline in 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in residential construction starts below 2000 thousand units signals weakening housing demand, which reduces confidence in broader consumer spending and triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 2000.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal produces positive returns in more than 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in industrial production and rise in the unemployment rate indicates a contraction in manufacturing output and labor market stress, signaling an impending economic slowdown that depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 100.0 and UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or the joint signal fails to achieve a Rank IC > 0.05 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains above 3.0% year-over-year, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and CPIAUCSL > 3.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal generates positive returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a drop in GDP growth (GDPC1), indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS < 12-month MA and GDPC1 < 0.5 (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to outperform baseline in 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% combined with stagnant payroll growth signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer confidence and corporate hiring, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5.0 and PAYEMS growth < 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal produces positive returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production below 100.0, coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0%, indicates a supply-side contraction and labor market stress, which signals an imminent economic downturn and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 100.0 and UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to achieve a Rank IC > 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
